summary: Low-risk PR integration and production deployment are separate opt-in actions.

g1.necessity: Reduce repeated human merge handoffs: ordinary low-risk PRs with protected CI should merge automatically without restarting or deploying services.

g2.authority_owner: GitHub protected main branch, pinned required CI Apps, existing MergeQueueStore flock
g2.non_duplication: No new signer, branch-protection mutation, release controller or deployment authority. GitHub's SHA-pinned protected merge endpoint remains the final authority.

model_evidence: PR86 and PR88 incident review showed excessive queue-only transitions, expiring Reviewer/Host evidence and redundant deployment coupling.
35 targeted positive and negative tests cover stale SHA, trusted CI, high-risk path refusal, shared merge-slot locking and post-merge verification.
g3.recovery_or_reason: Any high-risk path, incomplete CI, stale head/base, untrusted App, protection drift or occupied merge slot returns HOLD/WAIT without merging. Unknown merge outcome is not reported as success.

g4.rollback: Revert this isolated PR through normal protected GitHub PR. The tool is opt-in, default read-only, and does not alter any service or branch-protection settings.
verification: Ruff, targeted pytest, A.5 exact changed-path coverage, original complete R9 and remote CI.
Read-only live PR86 must HOLD as high risk; low-risk fixture must merge only with all five trusted checks and exact SHA.
No code path may call service_control, restart, deploy or publish production.

components.disposition: Opt-in low-risk PR readiness and protected GitHub merge with exact SHA, trusted CI, shared queue flock, no deploy.
evidence: New opt-in CLI and 35 focused tests; no existing production/Host code changed.
components.verification_level: Local targeted tests, Ruff, A.5, complete R9 and remote CI before protected merge.
components.model_evidence_veto_recovery_exit: Missing or contradictory evidence means HOLD; high-risk changes remain on independent Host review path.
components.rollback_route: Protected GitHub revert; no deployment rollback necessary because this PR does not deploy.
